title: musubi.errors/1
description: Every way musubi can fail, as the name it prints before the first colon on standard error. Published because a program driving musubi folds failures by that name and keeps nothing else from the line -- a message may quote a path from the machine musubi ran on. The set is closed and checked against the code: a kind that can reach standard error and is not listed fails musubi's own build (ADR-0046). SHAPE ONLY: this describes the document's structure and not the contract. That the list is COMPLETE -- that no kind musubi can print is missing from it -- is the thing the catalogue exists for, and it is a statement about musubi that no schema can express. musubi checks it against its own source; a consumer takes it on the same terms as the rest of docs/contracts.md.

contract.description: The identifier and its version. `-draft` says the freeze has not happened: a field may still change meaning. Once frozen, a field is never removed and never changes meaning, and adding one produces musubi.errors/2 rather than a quietly wider /1 (ADR-0024).

by.description: Which musubi wrote this: `musubi/<version>`. A reader comparing two catalogues needs to know which one is older before deciding that a kind was added.

errors.description: One entry per kind, in the order musubi lists them. MAY BE EMPTY: a library that makes no named failure has an empty array as its correct answer, not a missing field.

open_namespaces.description: Prefixes for kinds assembled at run time out of somebody else's vocabulary, so that a reader can recognise one it has never seen. musubi assembles none and this is empty; empty is an answer, and an absent field is a shrug.

kind.description: Exactly what is printed before the first colon on standard error. This is the whole of the interface: everything after the colon is for a person and may quote a path, so a reader that keeps failures should keep this and drop the rest.

exit_code.description: The code that always accompanies this kind. 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 refused. NOT 0: a kind that exits 0 is not a failure.

outcome.description: What happened, in a word an exit code cannot carry. musubi produces only `refused` and `failed`: it reads a folder that is already on the disk (ADR-0007), so there is no service to be unavailable and nothing to time out. The other two are in the enum because the vocabulary is the family's, not musubi's.

retryable.description: Whether asking again, unchanged, could do anything. False for everything musubi does except the file system itself, and for the same reason as above: there is no transient failure to wait out. A caller that retries a `refused` retries it forever.

detail.description: One line in English, to print under the kind. NOT A TEMPLATE: it holds no `{}` and no example path, because a reader with a log in front of it fills those in and then the log has the value in it.

detail_ja.description: The same line in Japanese, written by musubi rather than translated downstream. Two sentences written by one hand cannot disagree; a translation maintained by the reader drifts from the thing it describes the first time either changes.
